 OC Sheriff's deputy and special officer placed on leave. Video shows them talking with ICE agents
 Destiny Torres 
 covers all things SoCal, from breaking news to local government, with a focus on Orange County.
 Published November 16, 2026 at 4:19 PM PST
 An Orange County Sheriffs deputy walks into the Intake and Release center at the the Orange County Central Men's Jail in Santa Ana. ( Allen J. Schaben / Getty Images )
 One year ago, Congress defunded public media. Now that we're 100% community funded, please become a sustaining member or increase your existing membership today .
 At least two employees of the Orange County Sheriff’s Department are on administrative leave as the department investigates a report that a deputy and sheriff’s special officer were seen communicating with ICE agents, according to OCSD.
 The department on Friday pointed to surveillance video from Oct. 31 that was taken outside the Orange County Jail. It shows two OCSD employees “appearing to have a five-second conversation” with ICE agents in an unmarked vehicle parked outside the Orange County jail, according to the department. The conversation took place minutes before a man, who was hiding in the public courtyard, was arrested by the agents.
 State sanctuary law, known as the California Values Act , limits police cooperation with federal immigration agents and prohibits state and local law enforcement from investigating or arresting people for immigration enforcement purposes.
 Sheriff Don Barnes said in a statement that the department does not enforce federal immigration law but that he will fully cooperate with ICE to the extent the law allows.
 “Personnel acting outside the law and department policy will be held appropriately accountable,” Barnes said.
 He added the department will enforce state and local laws equally, without bias and without concern for anyone’s citizenship.
 Carlos Perea, executive director of the Harbor Institute for Immigrant and Economic Justice, told LAist this incident shows OCSD’s culture.
 Sponsored message 
 “The department has expressed time and time again that they will work with ICE to the fullest extent of the law,” Perea said. “OC Sheriff Barnes should use this as a learning lesson to end all collaboration with ICE.”
 Hector Bustos, communications director for political organizing group Chispa, told LAist he’s glad to see an investigation launched, but he’s not completely surprised by the incident.
 “We have known for a very long time that the Orange County Sheriff's Department has had a very close relationship with ICE,” Bustos said. “Our hope is that there is an independent investigation here because we know that historically when law enforcement agencies are investigating themselves, we don't see accountability.”
 OC Supervisor Vicente Sarmiento said he’s encouraged by the investigation, but that anxiety among residents is already heightened by the presence of ICE.
 “What it does is it chills the average person from wanting to trust law enforcement when it comes to becoming a witness to a crime, or as a victim to a crime,” Sarmiento said. “The average person may not know state law and just believes that there is collaboration because you see many times federal agents calling local law enforcement for assistance.”
 OC Supervisor Doug Chaffee, in a statement to LAist, welcomed the investigation and said any action that undermines trust or creates fear is concerning.
 “Our local law enforcement agencies should not be participating in federal immigration enforcement,” Chaffee said. “Orange County must remain committed to protecting our residents, upholding California law, and ensuring that local law enforcement remains focused on public safety – not federal immigration enforcement.”
 Sponsored message 
 LAist is working to reach the family of the man who was arrested in the surveillance video.
